description: The Arm-Co-Operator is a "newspaper published every two weeks, by the Personnel Publications Department of the Personal Service Division of the American Rolling Mill Company at Middletown, Ohio, for all Armco Men and Women." The Arm-Co-Operator covers news and events from all of the Armco plants, including: safety, personnel, training classes, clubs and sports activities, health and first aid, celebrations, vacations, births, marriages, deaths, illnesses, recipes, jokes, editorials, and classified ads. This issue's front page articles focus on: Nellis teams all taking first place in the Coal Riving Mining Institute's Fifth Annual First Aid Contest; Ashland welding section and riggers breaking new safety records; Miss Ruth Simukka in the Cleveland Office having left for the West Coast, where she will spend the coming year; Harry Holiday, General Superintendent, Columbia Division; Middletown Armco having a baseball victory over Cheviot, giving Middletown a chance to compete for the K. I. O. championship; regular dividend stock information from the General Office; production records being broken, as groups strive for new honors; an editorial titled, "Yield"; the world's first metal base highway was completed in Springfield, Illinois, in an experiment using Armco Ingot Iron in sheets and plates; the Butler Armco baseball team winning a victory; and, following a conference, W. L. Allen, President of the Sheffield Steel Corporation, flying from the Middletown airport to Kansas City, aboard an airplane outfitted for his convenience, with a business desk to allow for work while traveling.
